notes.made: Daryl Hall wrote it and Hall & Oates recorded it in 1980 for Voices as a churchy, organ-led soul song. Laurie Latham produced Young's version and rebuilt it around echoed piano, the Yamaha DX7 harp preset, Pino Palladino's fretless bass, and John Turnbull on Coral electric sitar and Spanish guitar. Ian Kewley played piano and synths, Mark Pinder drums.
notes.context: It reached 4 in Britain in March 1985 and The Secret of Association went to number 1. Young sang it at Live Aid on 13 July and it was number 1 on the Hot 100 two weeks later, and won British Video of the Year at the 1986 Brits. Hall said he'd only thought of it as a gospel and soul song until Young's version, which kept the elements but made it sound like a pop record.

listen_for.note: The plucked shimmer is the DX7's harp preset, sitting on top of the echoed piano.

listen_for.where: the bass line in every verse
listen_for.note: Pino Palladino's fretless, sliding into notes and answering Young's lines.
John Turnbull's Coral electric sitar, with his Ovation Spanish guitar alongside.

notes.unverified: Desmond's quote (US number 1, fretless bass, a Hall & Oates song) checks out. The Hall & Oates original is titled 'Everytime You Go Away'; Young's is 'Every Time You Go Away'.
